title: Names for Doers
objectives: I can tell that -er at the end of a word can mean a person who does something.
I can find the base word in farmer, builder, painter, writer, singer, and dancer.
I can use these words to tell about workers and artists.
I can make a new -er word and tell what it means.
rationale: The suffix -er is one of the two word patterns first graders can build on their own. Each word is a base children already know (farm, build, paint, write, sing, dance) plus -er, so they learn that -er names a person who does the action. Two spelling changes appear naturally (write plus -er is writer, dance plus -er is dancer), which gives a first look at dropping a final e. The unit revisits unlock, imagine, and habitat, because children use the un- idea from unit 8 to peel a prefix off a word and then do the same with a suffix, and because farmers and builders work in a habitat.

words.def: A person who grows crops and raises animals.
words.ex: The farmer got up early to milk the cows.
words.ex2: A farmer sold fresh corn at the market.

segs.m: land where crops and animals are raised

words.rel: people who make or grow things

apps.academic: A farmer plants seeds in the spring.
apps.writing: Tell what a farmer grows or raises.

cloze.s: The ___ planted corn seeds in long rows in the field.

cloze2.s: Every morning the ___ fed the chickens and the cows.

misuse.s: The farmer built a tall skyscraper in the middle of the city.
misuse.why: A farmer grows crops and raises animals. Building a skyscraper is not a farmer's job.

visual.alt: A farmer standing in a field of corn.

words.def: A person whose job is to make houses.
words.ex: The builder put a roof on the new house.
words.ex2: My uncle is a builder who made our treehouse.
words.rel: people who make or grow things

apps.academic: A builder follows a plan to make a house.

cloze.s: The ___ used a hammer and nails to put up the wooden wall.

cloze2.s: The ___ checked the plans before he began to work on the house.

misuse.s: The builder made the house by singing to the bricks.
misuse.why: A builder uses tools and materials to make a house. Singing does not build a house.

visual.alt: A worker in a helmet next to a house.

words.def: A person who makes pictures with colors.
words.ex: The painter used red and blue to make a sunset.
words.ex2: The painter stood on a ladder to color the wall.
words.rel: people who make or grow things

apps.academic: A painter mixes colors to make a new one.

cloze.s: The ___ mixed red and yellow to make orange for her picture.

cloze2.s: A ___ hung her picture of a cat in the art show.

misuse.s: The painter made a song and never used any colors.
misuse.why: A painter makes pictures with colors. Making only a song is not what a painter does.

visual.alt: An artist holding a paint palette.

words.def: A person who makes up stories or books.
words.ex: The writer thought of a funny story about a frog.
words.ex2: My aunt is a writer, and her book is about space.

morph.note: The final e of write is dropped: write + er becomes writer.

words.rel: people who make or grow things

apps.academic: A writer thinks of the characters first.
apps.spoken: I want to be a writer.

cloze.s: The ___ typed the last page of her new storybook.

cloze2.s: A ___ thinks of funny characters before starting a new book.

misuse.s: The writer finished the story by kicking a soccer ball.
misuse.why: A writer makes a story with words. Kicking a ball does not write anything.

visual.alt: A hand holding a pen beside a stack of books.

words.def: A person who makes music with their voice.
words.ex: The singer sang a happy song for the class.
words.ex2: My sister is a singer in the school choir.

apps.academic: A singer follows the tune and the words.
apps.writing: Tell what a singer does with a voice.

cloze.s: The ___ stood on the stage and filled the hall with her voice.

cloze2.s: A choir needs a ___ who can hit the high notes.

misuse.s: The singer stayed silent all night and never made a sound.
misuse.why: A singer makes music with a voice. Staying silent is not singing.

visual.alt: A microphone with music notes floating beside it.

words.def: A person who moves to music.
words.ex: The dancer jumped and spun on the stage.
words.ex2: A dancer in a bright dress twirled across the floor.

morph.note: The final e of dance is dropped: dance + er becomes dancer.

cloze.s: The ___ spun across the stage to the beat of the drum.

cloze2.s: A ___ practices every day so her steps are smooth.

misuse.s: The dancer sat perfectly still and never moved to the music.
misuse.why: A dancer moves to music. Sitting still is not dancing.

visual.alt: A dancer in a red dress with music notes.

passage.title: Doers in Our Town
paras: In our town, a farmer grows corn in a big field. A builder uses wood and nails to make a new house. A painter colors the walls, and a writer tells a story about the town. At night, a singer and a dancer share a show. Each person does something they love.

qs.why: The story says a builder makes a new house.

qs.q: Who shares a show at night?
qs.why: The story says a singer and a dancer share a show at night.

qs.q: In the story, what does a writer do?
qs.why: The story says a writer tells a story about the town.

write.prompt: Draw a person who does a job or hobby you like. Name the person with an -er word.

study.task: Cover -er at the end of each word. What base word is left? For writer and dancer, add back the e. Tell what each person does.

groups.label: people who make or grow things

sentences: Say what a farmer does each day.
Write a sentence about a builder and a house.
Tell what you would do if you were a singer or a dancer.

given: He is very good at it.
combine.model: Dan is a painter, and he is very good at it.
Mia is a writer, and many children read her stories.

discuss: Which -er job would you like to try? Why?
What other -er words do you know, like teacher or helper?
produce.explain: Explain what the -er in builder tells you. Use the word builder.

constructed.prompt: Tell what a farmer does and what a builder does.
constructed.model: A farmer grows food. A builder makes houses.

constructed.prompt: Tell about a singer and a dancer at a show.
constructed.model: The singer used her voice to make music. The dancer moved to the music.

teacher.overview: Children learn that -er at the end of a word can name a person who does something, then use six -er words to talk about workers and artists. The unit revisits unlock, imagine, and habitat.

notes.va.farmer.n: Start with farm plus -er. Ask what a farmer grows and raises. Not every -er word names a person (a ruler, a computer), so stay with people for now.
notes.va.builder.n: Build plus -er. Show a picture of a house being made. Children may say builder for anyone who plays with blocks; accept it as a good start.
notes.va.painter.n: Paint plus -er. A painter can make pictures or paint walls; here we use the picture sense. Link to colors and shiny from earlier.
notes.va.writer.n: Write plus -er, with the e dropped. Say write, then cover the e and add -er. Link to author as a close word.
notes.va.singer.n: Sing plus -er. Be careful with the g sound; singer rhymes with ringer. Play a short song and ask 'Who is the singer?'.
notes.va.dancer.n: Dance plus -er, with the e dropped. Act out a dancer. Link to the movement words from unit 7.

teacher.model: Think-aloud: 'The word is dancer. I see dance at the start and -er at the end. Dance means to move to music. -er means a person who does it. So a dancer is a person who moves to music. I can do the same with writer: write plus -er is a person who writes.'
discuss: Who do you know that is a farmer, builder, or painter?
What would you be if you could be any -er?
misconceptions: Every word that ends in -er names a person (water, paper, and sister do not follow this pattern).
-er means to do a thing more.
Only grown-ups can be a singer or a dancer.
extend: Children make a new -er word from a verb they know (jumper, helper, reader) and draw the person.
Play 'Who Am I?': a child acts out a job and others name the -er word.
teacher.reviewAdvice: Revisit the -er pattern the next day with new base words, again at one week, and look for -er words in read-alouds. The -er idea returns in grade 2 when children meet -est and -ly.

wida.oral: Partner A says a verb (build, write, sing). Partner B adds -er, names the person, and says what the person does.

needsReview: Spanish glosses (granjero, constructor, pintor, escritor, cantante, bailarín) are not reviewed by a native speaker; farmer may be agricultor in some regions.
Passage claims (farmers grow corn, builders make houses) are general facts.
Morphology notes: the e is dropped in writer and dancer; the base meanings in morph are simple first-grade wordings.
